subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should OpenClaw keep treating fenced `MEDIA:` lines as code examples and add warn-only diagnostics, or change the parser to extract those lines as media?
rationale: Both behaviors are plausible, but they trade off safe code examples against recovering common model output mistakes; current review discussion favors a delivery-boundary warning but maintainer intent is still required before merging the linked PR.

options.title: Warn Only At Delivery Boundary
options.body: Preserve current fenced-code semantics and emit one warning when a user-visible delivery path would otherwise show a skipped fenced `MEDIA:` line.

options.title: Extract From Fences
options.body: Treat standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines as intended attachments, accepting the risk that documentation or code examples can become media sends.

options.title: Docs Only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document that legacy `MEDIA:` lines must be standalone plain text.

recommendation.title: Warn Only At Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Preserve current fenced-code semantics and emit one warning when a user-visible delivery path would otherwise show a skipped fenced `MEDIA:` line.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc already reviewed the linked PR and framed the parser-purity versus delivery-warning boundary that maintainers need to settle.
